title: Xiaomi Quietly Ships MiMo-V2.5-DFlash
hook: Xiaomi quietly uploaded a speculative-decoding-style variant of its 300B+ MiMo-V2.5 model that could roughly double consumer-hardware throughput - once software catches up.
key_points: Xiaomi uploaded MiMo-V2.5-DFlash to Hugging Face with no announcement - a dedicated variant of its 300B+ parameter MiMo-V2.5 model.
The base MiMo-V2.5 already runs at roughly 8-10 tokens/sec on consumer hardware: two 24GB GPUs plus VRAM offload to 96-128GB of system RAM.
DFlash centers on a shared 'MTP' (multi-token-prediction) head, a speculative-decoding-style mechanism predicting several tokens per step.
Community estimates DFlash could roughly double throughput on the same hardware, but it wasn't yet working in llama.cpp at time of posting.
The mechanism and exact speedup are community speculation from a Reddit report, not confirmed benchmarks from Xiaomi.
content_html: Xiaomi, better known for phones than frontier LLMs, has quietly been building a serious open-weight model line - and just as quietly uploaded MiMo-V2.5-DFlash to Hugging Face with no announcement. It's a dedicated variant of MiMo-V2.5, a 300B+ parameter model that a LocalLLaMA user reports already runs at roughly 8-10 tokens/sec on consumer hardware (two 24GB GPUs plus VRAM offload to 96-128GB of system RAM).
extra_html: DFlash is built around a shared multi-token-prediction (MTP) head - a speculative-decoding-style mechanism that predicts several tokens per forward pass instead of one - and the poster speculates it could roughly double throughput on the same consumer setup. As of the report, though, DFlash support wasn't yet working in llama.cpp, and Xiaomi hasn't published official benchmarks or documentation, so the exact mechanism and expected speedup remain community speculation. See the original report and model card via the source link.
